prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a downward-angled egocentric view where the seated camera wearer's own body parts—a bent knee in frames 1–2, raised hands holding a plastic sheet in frame 3, and an outstretched left forearm in frames 4–5—are closest at roughly 0.2 to 0.5 metres (brightest white), positioned above and in front of flat wooden trays resting on the ground about 0.7 to 1.2 metres below (darker grey). No other people are present in the scene, so all visible limbs belong to the camera wearer facing downward, and both the held plastic wrapper (0.3–0.4 metres away) and the nearby trays of white patterned items (within 0.6–0.9 metres) are within or just at the edge of arm's reach, situated less than 0.5 metres from the wearer's knees and feet. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's knee in the lower center of frames 1–2 is replaced in frame 3 by the left arm and plastic sheet rising into the foreground and occluding the trays below, followed in frames 4–5 by the left arm extending diagonally from the middle-left toward the lower-right over the wearer's lap and bare right foot. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground plane of the translucent plastic sheet and outstretched arm from the recessed ground plane and tray edges beneath them. However, the map is unreliable regarding fine surface relief, as it completely flattens the raised 3D contours of the individual white piped shapes on the trays and smooths over the boundary between the plastic sheet and the right hand in frame 3.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map partitions the downward view into foreground body masks and background surface masks, though only the camera wearer is present (no other people face or look toward the camera) with body parts positioned 0.2 to 0.6 metres away and ground trays 0.7 to 1.2 metres below. In frames 1–2, a large teal mask labeled 'bed' covers the wooden trays in the upper and middle regions while leaving the wearer's green-clothed knee at the bottom center (0.3 metres away) unsegmented in black; in frame 3, brown, pink, and light-blue 'person' masks capture the left arm, lap, and right fingers holding a plastic sheet (0.3–0.4 metres away, within arm's reach) around a central blue 'cake' mask. Across frames 4–5, as the wearer's left forearm shifts from the lower-left to stretch diagonally across the frame and partially occlude the lower trays and lap, a pink 'person' mask tracks the arm while purple and green 'donut' masks appear on the rightmost tray in frame 5 (about 0.7 metres away and 0.3 metres right of the arm). While the segmentation map helps isolate the boundary of the wearer's diagonally extended forearm against the cluttered background in frames 4–5 better than a quick glance at the RGB, it is highly unreliable in both class labels and spatial completeness. Specifically, it misclassifies the drying trays of food items as 'bed' and 'donut' and the plastic wrapper as 'cake' and 'person', merges the wearer's green trousers with the held plastic in frame 3, and completely misses the trays in frame 4 as well as the knee in frames 1–2.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five-frame strip, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand in the upper-left-of-center region of frame 3 at roughly 0.3 to 0.4 metres from the camera, with no other people present in the scene. In frame 3, this detected left hand is positioned above the wearer's lap and about 0.2 metres to the left of the partially visible right hand at the right edge, within immediate reach of the held plastic sheet and about 0.5 metres above the wooden trays on the ground. Across the sequence, no skeletons are rendered during the knee-dominated views of frames 1–2 or when the left forearm extends downward and rightward across the lower-left and center of frames 4–5 (where the hands are cropped out of the frame boundaries). This map makes the exact 3D articulation of the curled fingers and thumb of the wearer's left hand pinching the top edge of the plastic wrapper in frame 3 much easier to see than in the RGB image. However, the pose map is largely unreliable for broader spatial understanding because it fails to fit a yellow body skeleton to the visible knee, torso, bare foot, or outstretched forearm in any frame, and it misses the partially visible right fingers at the upper-right edge of frame 3.
